bottom_line: In patients with heart failure and left ventricular ejection fraction of 0.45 or less, digoxin vs placebo did not affect all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.99; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.91 to 1.07).
implications: These data support that, in the main trial, digoxin reduced hospitalization for worsening heart failure (26.8% vs 34.7%; risk ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.79) without reducing all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.07). The results also indicate a higher risk of hospitalization for suspected digoxin toxicity with digoxin (2.0% vs 0.9%; risk ratio, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.42 to 3.32).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing digoxin vs placebo added to diuretics and ACE inhibitors, with average follow-up 37 months.
major_points.quote: We studied the effect of digoxin on mortality and hospitalization in a randomized, double-blind clinical trial.

major_points.text: Main trial enrolled patients with LVEF ≤0.45 and normal sinus rhythm; 3397 assigned to digoxin and 3403 to placebo.
